title: Setting Up Business Manager the Right Way
subtitle: A safe home for your Page, ad account and Pixel
youtube_title: How to Set Up Meta Business Manager (Business Portfolio) the Right Way | Meta Ads Course Lesson 2
description: Lesson 2 of the free Meta Ads course. Business Manager, now called a business portfolio, is the home for everything you run ads with. In this lesson: why you should not run ads from a personal ad account, how to create a business portfolio, which assets to add, how to give people the right access, and the security settings that protect your account.

slides.narration: Hi, I'm Khalil Baghirov, and welcome to lesson two of this free Meta Ads course. In lesson one we saw how the ad auction works. Today we build the foundation: Business Manager. Set it up right once, and you avoid lost accounts, locked pages, and a lot of stress later.

slides.text: Business Manager is now a *business portfolio*
slides.narration: First, a quick note on the name. Meta now calls Business Manager a business portfolio, and you manage it inside Meta Business Suite. Many people still say Business Manager, and that's fine. It's the same idea: one central place that owns your business assets, separate from your personal profile.

slides.title: Personal ad account vs business portfolio
bad: Profile issue can stop your ads
good: Give each person only the access they need
Easy to add a freelancer or agency
slides.narration: Why does this matter? A personal ad account is tied to one personal profile. It is hard to share access safely, and if that profile has a problem, your ads can stop. In a business portfolio, the business owns the assets. You give each person only the access they need, and it's easy to add a freelancer or agency, then remove them later.

slides.title: Create your business portfolio
items: Enter your business name and email
slides.narration: Creating one takes a few minutes. Go to business dot facebook dot com and log in with your real personal profile. Choose create a business portfolio. Enter your business name, your name, and your business email. Then confirm the email address from the message Meta sends you. If you already have a portfolio, skip this step and open business settings instead.

slides.title: Add your assets
slides.narration: Next, add your assets in the business settings. Connect your Facebook Page and your Instagram account. Add an ad account, either your existing one or a new one created inside the portfolio. Create a Pixel or dataset, which we will install in a later lesson. And finally add a payment method, so the ad account can actually run. Only add assets your business really owns.

slides.title: Give people the right access
items: Two trusted admins with full control
Assign only the assets each person needs
Remove people when the work ends
slides.narration: Now people and access. Always have two trusted admins with full control, so one lost login never locks you out. Give partial access to everyone else, like employees or freelancers. Assign only the assets each person needs, for example just the ad account, not the Page. And remove people when the work ends.

slides.title: Protect your account
items: Require it for everyone in the portfolio
slides.narration: Finally, protect your account. Turn on two-factor authentication on your own profile. In security settings you can require it for everyone in the portfolio. Never share your password; share access instead. And ignore fake Meta warning messages that ask you to log in through a strange link. That is the most common way pages get stolen.

slides.title: Your homework
items: Create or open your business portfolio
Add your Page, Instagram and ad account
Add a second admin and turn on two-factor authentication
slides.narration: Your homework for today. Create or open your business portfolio. Add your Page, Instagram, and ad account. Then add a second admin and turn on two-factor authentication. It takes fifteen minutes and can save your business.

slides.next: Campaigns, Ad Sets and Ads: Account Structure
slides.narration: In the next lesson, we will look at account structure: campaigns, ad sets, and ads, and what you control at each level. Subscribe so you don't miss it, and I'll see you in lesson three.
